newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends up as distillate stock draw seen.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends up as distillate stock draw seen.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended higher Wednesday on expectations that weekly oil inventory data would show a decline in distillate stocks following last week's frigid temperatures in the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States.
"The action was due to API expectations which caused shorts to cover," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst with Cargill Investor Services Inc in New York.
Feb heat settled up 0.86 cent at 66.89 cents a gallon. Feb gasoline ended up 0.78 cent at 68.22 cents a gallon, and March crude finished two cents higher at $24.24 a barrel.

Traders expected Wednesday evening's weekly oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show that distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, to have dropped by about three million barrels.
After the market's close, the API said distillate stocks declined 2.95 million barrels.
Dealers said last week's cold snap in the Northeast that sent temperatures 15 to 20 degrees below normal heightened heat demand in the world's largest market for heating oil.
High import levels were expected to have boosted crude and gasoline stocks by more than one million barrels in the stock data which reflects the week ended January 17.
The data in fact showed a decline in crude stocks of 3.42 million barrels while gasoline stocks rose 3.03 million barrels.
Crude and gasoline prices rose despite expected increases in supply as a fire at Tosco Corp's Avon refinery in California late Tuesday threatened decreased production.
An explosion at a 32,000 barrel per day (bpd) gasoline making unit set Tosco's Avon refinery ablaze. The refinery has a capacity of 156,000 bpd.
A Tosco spokesman said the hydrocracker would be down "for some time."
But, dealers said the fire was relatively small and the refinery was outside the U.S. supply region directly affecting NYMEX contracts, so it would not have a long term impact.

"This rally was partly news driven by the Tosco fire, but a West Coast refinery really doesn't have anything to do with the East Coast products market," said Al Lindseth, manager of oil and gas hedge programs at GSC Energy in Atlanta.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
